certification.name: PyTorch Core: Practical ML & Neural Networks

concepts.name: CrossEntropyLoss
concepts.description: `nn.CrossEntropyLoss` accepts unnormalized class logits and, for the common class-index case, integer targets containing class indices.

concepts.name: BCEWithLogitsLoss
concepts.description: `nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss` combines sigmoid behavior with binary cross-entropy in a numerically stable formulation.

concepts.name: MSELoss
concepts.description: `nn.MSELoss` measures mean squared error between input and target values when using its default mean reduction.

concepts.name: L1Loss
concepts.description: `nn.L1Loss` measures absolute elementwise error and is less dominated by large individual errors than squared-error loss.

concepts.name: SGD optimizer
concepts.description: `torch.optim.SGD` implements stochastic gradient descent and can add options such as momentum and weight decay.

concepts.name: AdamW optimizer
concepts.description: `torch.optim.AdamW` implements AdamW, where weight decay is decoupled from the momentum and variance updates.

concepts.name: Weight decay
concepts.description: `weight_decay` is an optimizer regularization hyperparameter that penalizes large weights according to the optimizer algorithm.

concepts.name: Learning-rate schedulers
concepts.description: PyTorch learning-rate schedulers modify optimizer learning rates according to a schedule or monitored metric.

concepts.name: ReduceLROnPlateau
concepts.description: `ReduceLROnPlateau` lowers the learning rate when a monitored metric stops improving for the configured patience.

questions.explanation: nn.CrossEntropyLoss accepts unnormalized class logits and, for the common class-index case, integer targets containing class indices. For logits shaped [N, C], a common target shape is [N] with class ids from 0 to C-1. Do not apply softmax to logits before CrossEntropyLoss; the loss expects logits directly.
hints: For logits shaped [N, C], a common target shape is [N] with class ids from 0 to C-1.

questions.explanation: PyTorch learning-rate schedulers modify optimizer learning rates according to a schedule or monitored metric. Many epoch-based schedulers use scheduler.step() after the intended training epoch boundary. Scheduler step timing depends on the scheduler type; metric-based schedulers such as ReduceLROnPlateau need a metric value.
hints: Many epoch-based schedulers use scheduler.step() after the intended training epoch boundary.
